page: Amazon Web Services i7i.16xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processors built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 virtual CPUs, corresponding to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 2.4 GHz. The processor is equipped with a 320 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. The hardware configuration includes 512.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is bundled with 15,000 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is delivered via a 38 Gbps baseline bandwidth managed by the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core processing capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25%. Single-core performance is moderate, categorized in the middle 50% by stress-ng, though Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics reach the top 10%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks show strong performance, as do data operations like Redis SET, which achieves 87.75 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput is highly efficient, ranking in the top 10%. For machine learning workloads, LLM inference speeds for prompt processing and text generation on small to medium models remain strong, though text generation on large 70B models drops to average levels.

Given the massive 15 TB local NVMe SSD storage and 512 GB DDR5 RAM, this server offers high resource density for data-intensive operations. The qualitative cost efficiency is driven by the integration of large-capacity local storage directly with high-bandwidth memory, reducing the need for external storage attachments. This configuration is suitable for large-scale databases, Redis caching layers, data warehousing, and high-throughput web serving. It is also capable of handling software compilation and moderate LLM inference tasks, though it lacks dedicated GPU hardware for heavy deep learning training.
